_comment: Gallery images for the GREAT Greenland ROV site. To add a photo: commit the image file into this images/ folder, then add an entry to the list below. The gallery on the homepage renders these in order.

photos.caption: Operator winching the ROV down for the first dive.
The ROV aboard the RV Celtic Explorer in Iceland before departure.
The ROV being loaded for transport from Limerick at the start of operations.
The team monitoring a dive from the ROV control cabin.
Live camera and sonar feeds from Étaín on the seabed. The green lasers give scale.
Operating the manipulators to collect a core sample.
Flying Étaín from OceanRINGS autopilot control software.
The team following the dive from the control container.
Pre-dive planning from the multibeam before the volcano dive.
Deep-sea animals spread out on the seabed, crossed by the green scaling lasers.
An animal lit by the ROV.
A colony rising from the seabed in the ROV's lights.
A rich seabed of animals captured from Étaín's camera at 855 m depth.
Multibeam sonar and the HD14K camera feed on the control-room screen during a dive.
Crew watching the multibeam sonar and live camera feeds from the control container.
Multibeam bathymetry of the Greenland Spreading Zone, showing the spreading directions and Louise's Fault.
Bathymetry of the Caldera, the underwater volcano surveyed on the mission.
Bathymetry of the isolated seamount, rising from ~1157 m at its base to ~658 m at its summit.
Bathymetry of the drowned valley — the up-slope transect dive.
Bathymetry of the drowned valley — the canyon dive.
Bathymetry of the fault line surveyed west of the Caldera.
